quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out of a parked car or between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their car without seeing you.

questions.question: A green arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may turn in that direction after stopping completely.
You cannot turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means traffic in that lane must go the direction the arrow points. Drivers turning on a green arrow have the right-of-way, but should still watch for pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Road work or maintenance is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. These signs help drivers and pedestrians stay safe in dangerous zones. Traffic fines may double in areas with these signs.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, always check behind you. Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Also check that no other driver is moving into the same spot from another lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: This black and yellow sign means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to road work.
The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign tells you to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should:

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign means a divided highway is starting and you should stay to the right.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take risky chances to pass you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road gets wider.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to conditions ahead and are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the right lane is ending and you should be ready for merging traffic.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, yield to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: After stopping completely, vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights on a school bus mean it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and careful. Slow down as you approach it.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They disappear if you have one mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars. Avoid driving in these areas.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Always signal when pulling next to a curb and when pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Highway pavement is most slippery:

options.text: After it has rained for several hours.
When rain first starts.
After it has rained for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a greasy, slippery surface.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: If you get tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you become tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the merge lane to speed up and match the traffic flow. Then merge smoothly when it is safe. Do not stop like you would on regular roads.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of work zones. Watch for orange signs, cones, or barrels while driving. Be ready for unexpected conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, why should you look far ahead of your vehicle?

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking far ahead helps you avoid sudden stops or lane changes. You can react early and drive safer. This also saves fuel and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic flows in both directions.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to reach your destination faster.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue: struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting from your lane, or turning up the radio. If you notice these signs, park safely and rest with a short nap.

questions.question: A car with bright headlights is driving toward you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is permitted on a green arrow only.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow-green warning signs alert you to upcoming conditions. This includes curves and sharp turns ahead.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may be merging into your lane ahead.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Do not stay beside them for long stretches.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: To spot potential hazards early.
Because your vehicle takes a quarter mile to stop completely.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic and signals from other drivers. Expect merging vehicles at ramps and be ready for rapid changes in road and traffic conditions.
